title: ERF 236150 Current Versus Proposed Rule Change and Impact Report
baseline_label: Ohio Laws effective text, live retrieved October 7, 2026
target_label: October 5, 2026 BIA/CSI referral draft; not operative
overview:
The October 5 BIA/CSI packet contains **nine proposed rule identifiers** across 62 PDF pages and prints an October 12, 2026 comment deadline. It is marked **DRAFT — NOT YET FILED**. The baseline is the effective Ohio Laws text retrieved October 7, 2026.

Key changes concern MH day-treatment counseling, PSR groups, collateral contacts, SUD assessment/attendance, and authorization dependencies. MH day treatment in October differs materially from September’s MH IOP/PHP model. TBS retains unlicensed qualification pathways. Draft cross-reference errors and residential coverage conflicts need clarification.

The October packet supplies **no fee appendix**. September’s proposed rates are historical scenario inputs, not confirmed October rates. Summaries and likely impacts follow; each rule links to separate full current/proposed text and a diff.
coverage_notes: Matched: 5160-8-05; 5160-27-01, -02, -04, -06, -08, -09, -10, and -14. ACT has an explicit rescind/replacement pair. Effective 5160-27-03, -11, -12, and -13 are not attached in the October packet and are not classified as repealed. September proposal -03 and -11 are outside the October draft comparison.

entries.title: Licensed-professional services and supervision
entries.summary: Supervision and documentation are clarified; proposed (B)(7) permits immediate availability via real-time audio-visual technology when allowed by the licensing board. Proposed (D)(1)(c)(iii) names CANS assessment coverage effective July 1, 2027. Proposed (D)(3) points future service limits to the 5160-1-31 appendix/Master List, and (E)(2) adds explicit recreational exclusions. Current (G)(2)(d) already pays general-supervision trainees at 85% of the supervising practitioner rate; the October draft retains that formula. It does not establish a new across-the-board trainee rate increase versus the current rule.
entries.impact: Agencies need board-specific supervision evidence and service-specific claim rules. Scope, payer implementation, and CANS rollout must be resolved before changing production claims. Forecast trainee reimbursement by supervisor tier and service; do not treat the retained 85% formula as a newly earned uplift.
entries.action: Credentialing/compliance: map supervision modality by licensing board. Billing/system owner: retain separate trainee direct/general-supervision logic and stage CANS changes for verified implementation.
entries.risk: The September draft contained an additional 72.25% general-supervision clause that is absent from the October attachment. Do not carry that conflicting September clause into the updated scenario.

entries.title: Eligible agencies, rendering providers, and supervisors
entries.summary: Proposed (A)(1) updates OhioMHAS to DBH and expressly ties agency services to the services/supports on DBH certifications and national accreditation standards. Proposed (A)(6) changes the supervisor reference from (D)(1)–(D)(17) to (D)(1)–(D)(16), excluding the listed certified peer supporter from that unlicensed-practitioner supervision reference. The broader (D) list still contains a certified peer supporter at (17). The BIA describes this rule mainly as an agency-name/typo update, but these text differences warrant operational review.
entries.impact: Agency certification scope and rendering-provider supervision assignments require reconciliation. A peer supervisor appearing on the general list does not by itself establish eligibility to supervise an (A)(6) QMHS/CMS under the narrowed cross-reference.
entries.action: Credentialing/clinical leadership: reconcile program certifications, accreditation scope, and supervisor assignments; confirm the intended treatment of peer supervision with ODM/DBH.
entries.risk: Distinguish the BIA narrative description from the actual proposed (A)(1) and (A)(6) text; do not dismiss these changes as clerical without review.

entries.title: Coverage, CPST transition, collateral contacts, and authorization dependencies
entries.summary: Current (B)(3) expressly covers CPST; the October proposal removes that standalone service from the listed coverage framework and lists TBS/PSR, ACT, MH day-treatment hourly/per-diem, nursing, testing, psychotherapy, and peers as potentially subject to limits in the 5160-1-31 appendix. Proposed (H)(1) replaces the current minimum-QMHS treatment-plan standard with a licensed-practitioner reference to 5160-27-01(D)(1)–(D)(6), while allowing supervised unlicensed participation. Proposed (K)(6) enumerates nonreimbursable supervision activities. Proposed (K)(7) permits same-organization collateral contact across different lines of business with consent/justification, treatment-plan purpose, documented benefit, and no concurrent billing by both providers.
entries.impact: CPST activities need a clinical service/activity crosswalk rather than automatic rebilling under another code. EHR workflows need consent, line-of-business identification, collateral purpose/outcome, and duplicate-contact edits. PA limits cannot be inferred from this packet because the controlling appendix is a separate package.
entries.action: Clinical/billing owners: map affected CPST encounters and validate collateral documentation. Compliance: seek clarification on treatment-plan author eligibility. Forecast owner: keep PA utilization assumptions editable until the separate appendix is available.
entries.risk: The (D)(1)–(D)(6) treatment-plan citation excludes later-listed independently licensed practitioners such as LISWs and LPCCs. Obtain clarification before interpreting the citation as an intended restriction. The separate Master List and payer implementation remain unresolved.

entries.title: ACT replacement and fidelity-dependent payment
entries.summary: The BIA expressly identifies rescission and replacement of ACT. The replacement uses DBH rule 5122-29-29 for service/fidelity requirements, retains member eligibility and the four-unit monthly structure, adds Master List dependency, and retains ODM payment suspension authority tied to fidelity. The complete replacement text is compared with the effective predecessor below; reduced rule length does not imply removal of incorporated DBH requirements.
entries.impact: Agencies need certification/fidelity evidence and coordinated enrollment/disenrollment records. Bundling and outpatient exclusivity continue to affect revenue outside ACT. Preserve clinical eligibility and team-category unit controls in the forecast.
entries.action: ACT program/compliance owner: reconcile the incorporated DBH standard, certification, fidelity monitoring, enrollment notice process, and maximum unit categories.
entries.risk: The replacement contains mismatched paragraph references: (H) refers to fidelity in (J)(1), but (J) is prescriber contact; (I)(3) refers to categories (L)(1)/(L)(2), which are nonbillable activities; (F)(2) refers to notifying ODM of enrollment after discharge. Treat these as draft clarification items.

entries.title: MH day-treatment hourly and per-diem group counseling
entries.summary: Current (B) uses a 2.5-hour daily split for hourly versus per diem and allows specified same-day services and some cross-provider billing with PA. The October draft reframes the service as the group-counseling component of multimodal MH day treatment: hourly reimbursement is capped at ten hours per week; full per diem requires at least 3.5 hours/day and 10.5 hours/week; at least one hour forty-five minutes but less than 3.5 hours permits 50% of the applicable provider-type per diem. Two consecutive weeks below 10.5 hours trigger rescission of existing authorization, with lower-level reimbursement not exceeding ten hours/week. Proposed (C)(2)(a)(i) delays licensed-only rendering to July 1, 2027; the 1:12 ratio remains. Proposed (D)(3) bars hourly and per-diem same-day reimbursement for the same member by any billing provider.
entries.impact: Revenue modeling must use delivered group-counseling minutes and weekly attendance, not total program attendance. Staffing costs require a transition-date scenario. The October service title and structure supersede the September draft assumption that the modeled MH services should be labeled IOP/PHP.
entries.action: Forecast owner: build MH hourly/per-diem counseling scenarios with the 1.75/3.5-hour half/full thresholds, ten-hour hourly cap, 10.5-hour weekly minimum, two-week attendance logic, 1:12 group ratio, and July 1, 2027 licensed-only transition. Billing: prepare cross-provider same-day review.
entries.risk: The eligibility reference to 5160-27-08(A)(2) appears stale after that rule is reorganized, and the between-ten-and-10.5-hours treatment/reimbursement boundary needs clarification. Dollar rates are not included in this October package.

entries.title: TBS and PSR activity remapping, qualification tiers, and groups
entries.summary: The October draft assigns shared treatment-planning, psychoeducation, and crisis-prevention activities to both TBS and PSR, then separates TBS evidence-informed symptom interventions from PSR functional rehabilitation. Proposed (C)(2) retains TBS eligibility for licensed or unlicensed practitioners with the degree pathway or a high-school diploma plus three years relevant experience; the current rule already has those alternatives. Proposed (D) adds functional-deficit member criteria and expressly includes licensed or unlicensed PSR rendering practitioners with population-specific training. Current (D)(3) prohibits group PSR; proposed (F)(4) allows it at 1:6. Proposed group TBS is less than 10.5 hours/week with a 1:12 ratio. PA limits move to the separate appendix.
entries.impact: TBS is not globally licensed-only under this attachment. Forecast eligible staffing by service and documented qualifications. PSR groups create a modeled service option but require clinical fit, ratio controls, group duration/units rules, and verified fee/PA implementation; activity remapping must remain clinically supported.
entries.action: Clinical/credentialing owners: map activities, eligibility, documented experience and population training. Forecast/system owner: add separate TBS and PSR groups with distinct ratios and threshold logic.
entries.risk: Proposed (E) defines collateral contact as interaction with a recipient who plays a significant role in a recipient’s life, rather than clear third-party language. Proposed (F)(4) cites (B)(1)(b)/(B)(1)(c), which do not exist in the revised shared-activity outline. Proposed (F)(1) still excludes SUD residential payment, conflicting with proposed 5160-27-09(C)(3)(h).

entries.title: SUD assessment, per-diem attendance, residential bundles, and ASAM evidence
entries.summary: The draft adds separate SUD level-of-care and treatment-planning assessments for ASAM 1, 2.1, and 2.5 apart from psychiatric diagnostic evaluation. Proposed (C)(2) defines group-counseling intensity and per-diem time, excludes breaks, and includes July 1, 2027 full/half daily thresholds: IOP 3h1m/1h31m and PHP 4h1m/2h1m. Proposed (E) requires dimensional risk ratings, treatment-goal linkage, baseline/interval validated measures, and outcome/discharge evidence. The residential per diem bundles listed core services while proposed (C)(3)(h) describes TBS, PSR, MH day treatment, ACT, and IHBT as eligible services, unlike the current noncovered list. Outside-per-diem providers must be unaffiliated and the service essential, medically necessary, and unable to wait for discharge. Proposed (F)(4) adds attendance downgrade and no additional same-day SUD group counseling; (F)(5) adds admission/discharge and same-organization transition billing rules.
entries.impact: Revenue forecasts need counted group minutes, interruption/break time, attendance downgrade logic, assessment assumptions, residential bundle exclusions, and separate outside-provider controls. Documentation changes require structured ASAM and outcome-measure evidence. Residential carve-outs cannot be modeled as confirmed collectible revenue while contradictory MH restrictions remain.
entries.action: SUD clinical/billing owners: build ASAM and assessment documentation checks, group-time/break tracking, attendance and transition edits. Forecast owner: stage 2027 minute thresholds, half-rate scenarios, and residential carve-outs as unresolved alternatives.
entries.risk: Proposed 5160-27-09(C)(3)(h) conflicts with continued SUD-residential exclusions in 5160-27-06(D)(1), 5160-27-08(F)(1), and ACT exclusivity. Other errors include the withdrawal-management reference to (B)(2)(e), which does not exist, and an IOP downgrade expression that says less than an average of nine to nineteen hours. Do not implement these literally without ODM clarification.

entries.title: SUD targeted case-management limits
entries.summary: The October proposal retains the core targeted-case-management activities, excludes QMHS and certified peer supporters as rendering practitioners, and retains residential bundling. Current (E) expressly requires PA for TCM when a member is enrolled in ACT or IHBT; proposed (E) instead refers additional scope, duration, frequency, and co-occurring-service limits to the 5160-1-31 appendix. Agency name and member terminology are also updated.
entries.impact: Removal of the specific PA sentence is not evidence that ACT/IHBT-related TCM becomes unrestricted. Qualified rendering-provider controls and residential bundling remain relevant.
entries.action: Billing/authorization owner: retain existing applicable payer controls until the finalized rule, appendix, and implementation instructions establish the replacement requirements.
entries.risk: The October package does not supply the new appendix limits; keep ACT/IHBT authorization and bundling outcomes unresolved in the proposed scenario.

entries.title: Peer-service authorization and MRSS exception
entries.summary: The proposal removes the current explicit more-than-four-hours/day PA sentence and references limitations in the 5160-1-31 appendix instead. The 1:12 peer-group ratio remains. Proposed (E)(1)(c) adds an MRSS exception for unrelated peer services already actively furnished by another billing provider before initiation of the regional mobile crisis response. Admission/discharge language for residential, inpatient, and PRTF exceptions changes from admission and discharge to admission or discharge.
entries.impact: Agencies need proof of preexisting peer-service relationships, separate billing providers, and the crisis initiation timeline before relying on the MRSS exception. Deleted four-hour language does not establish unlimited peer coverage.
entries.action: Peer program/billing owners: add documentation fields and a prebilling exception review for MRSS overlap; monitor the separate PA appendix and payer instructions.
entries.risk: The newer text does not provide replacement daily/hour limits or establish the operational claims edit for the MRSS exception.

afterword:
Use the per-rule next actions to assign clinical, credentialing, billing, authorization, and forecast work. Keep thresholds, staffing transitions, PA limits, and residential carve-outs as editable scenarios until finalized authority and payer implementation establish them.

[Thorough PDF parse audit](Parse_Audit_2026-10-08/README.md) inventories every page in both packets, preserves retained source spans and isolated numbers, and reconstructs the September fee appendix by cell. [Source validation](ERF236150_Source_Validation_2026-10-07.md) records the original extraction and current baseline. The official PDFs control exact layout. Cross-referenced DBH rules and the separate 5160-1-31 appendix require their own scoped review.
